en.name: Francis
en.summary: The first Jesuit pope and the first from the Americas, whose pontificate emphasized mercy, the poor, and care for the environment.
en.body: Jorge Mario Bergoglio, archbishop of Buenos Aires, took the name Francis in honor of St. Francis of Assisi and set a markedly informal tone from his first appearance, famously asking the crowd to pray for him before he blessed them. His pontificate centered on outreach to the marginalized, migrants, and the poor, and on the encyclical Laudato si', which framed environmental care as a moral and spiritual obligation. He also pursued reforms to Vatican finances and governance and took a more pastoral, less doctrinally rigid public tone than his immediate predecessors, generating both wide popularity and conservative criticism, until his death in 2025.
